Boaz R. Weinstein Signals Activist Plans at Destiny Tech100 with 7.58% Stake

Boaz R. Weinstein and Saba Capital Management, L.P. reported owning 3,611,594 shares of Destiny Tech100 Inc., equal to a 7.58% stake. Their Schedule 13D, filed Nov. 20, 2026, reports the position as of Nov. 18 and says they consider the shares undervalued. The investment could lead to discussions or proposals about the fund’s governance, strategy and future structure.

Investor Intent

Saba Capital says it bought the shares because it sees an attractive investment opportunity. The firm may discuss Destiny Tech100’s business, board appointments, governance and trading discount with company leaders and other shareholders, and it may make shareholder proposals or nominate directors.

Saba Capital may also seek share buybacks, tenders or liquidation, or push for changes to the company’s investment strategy, manager or open- or closed-end structure. The filing describes these as possible actions, not decisions the firm has already made.

Investor's Background

Saba Capital Management, L.P. is a Delaware limited partnership that manages private and public investment funds and accounts. Saba Capital Management GP, LLC, also organized in Delaware, serves as its general partner. Boaz R. Weinstein, a U.S. citizen, serves as managing member of the general partner.

data.title: Wintermute policy chief calls for crypto lobby to ‘clean house’ in D.C.
data.description:
Wintermute's head of policy and advocacy, Ron Hammond, urged the crypto industry to "clean" its house in Washington following what he called a series of lobbying setbacks amid policymaking.

Speaking at the Capital Crypto Forum on Thursday, Hammond said the industry has struggled to counter larger financial interests as tokenization brings crypto and traditional finance into direct competition.

"I would say we probably need to clean house a little bit on the policy side here," Hammond said. "There's been fractures in the industry that show that either A, we're not united enough, or B, when we go up against a larger force, we just don't win”

His comments come a month after the Securities and Exchange Commission in September introduced a five-year innovation exemption that opened a route for trading tokenized U.S. stocks.

However, the policy has drawn resistance from both traditional finance companies and lawmakers, with Hammud also having some reservations.

"We see it being really limited and tailored in its final form," he said. " But effectively, even for companies like us, it doesn't really do much good for us. I mean, the limits are pretty strong. So that's why we're saying it's a great first step, but we have a lot more ways to go here."

TradFi lobbying against tokenization

Dozens of major companies, including JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, and McDonald's, have objected to third-party tokenized versions of their shares under the SEC's exemption process.

"It's weird to see in New York, we are partnering with a lot of these firms that I'm lobbying against here in D.C. [...]," Hammond said. "We partner with the banks all the time, but in D.C. we are against them on a lot of fronts."

Hammond also criticized crypto's choice of political allies, saying some lawmakers who campaigned as pro-crypto later opposed tokenization.

Earlier this week, four Democratic senators, including Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto, warned SEC Chair Paul Atkins that the exemption left gaps around know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering requirements.

The SEC's tokenization exemption is also facing questions from within its incoming leadership. On Thursday, Kristin Johnson, Trump's Democratic pick for the commission, said at a Senate Banking Committee hearing that she would welcome a formal rulemaking process with public comment, given concerns raised by those opposing the rule.

Meanwhile, the industry also faces competition from other jurisdictions, Hammond said, as officials seek to attract digital-asset businesses.

"When I go over to the UK, they love to hear any moment that America has a gap. Like when Clarity failed, they were all asking me, 'What can we do to get these firms back to the UK?'"

data.title: Enel expands U.S. renewables portfolio with 317 MW solar deal
data.description:
Enel said Friday it agreed to acquire a portfolio of solar plants in the U.S. from clean energy infrastructure developer energyRe, boosting its installed renewable capacity in North America to 13.5 GW, including storage assets.

Enel said the plants, located in South Carolina, have a total installed capacity of 317 MW and an expected average annual electricity production exceeding 540 GWh.

Financial terms were not disclosed, but Enel said it expects the deal to increase its net financial debt by ~$255M once ​the plants ​are completed ⁠and considering the effects of their entry into service.

The company estimates the assets ​will ⁠generate an additional $30M in annual EBITDA after they become operational.

The deal is part of the strategy outlined at Enel's Capital Markets Day in February, which identified acquisitions of existing renewable assets in established markets as a way to expand generation capacity.

data.title: Stocks jump more than 10% six months after the VIX reaches 28-33
data.description:
When the CBOE Volatility Index closes around the 30 level, U.S. stocks tend to increase more than 10% in the following six months.

The VIX ended above 28 on Thursday, and it’s currently above 30, having increased more than 70% in the past month.

“Readings between 28 and 33 have historically proven a strong buying opportunity, with average six-month forward returns nearly +10%,” analysts at Finom Group noted.

The forward six-month S&P 500 (SP500) return when the volatility index is between 28.7 and 33.5 is currently implied to be 9.3%. When the VIX is above 33.5, S&P 500 (SP500) returns jump to 12.7% in the next six months.

“This is likely ‘peaking’ volatility, bottoming equity regime,” they said.

The S&P 500 (SP500) opened below the red line, currently at $7.144.41, down 0.4% in early morning trade. It has declined almost 3% in the past six months.

data.title: Urban Company Raises Rs 2,500 Cr Through QIP, Issue Subscribed Six Times
data.description:
The institutional placement attracted bids worth over Rs 15,000 crore, with 33 investors receiving share allotments at Rs 156 apiece

Home services platform Urban Company has raised Rs 2,500 crore through a Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP) of equity shares, with the issue receiving bids worth more than Rs 15,000 crore, around six times the issue size.

The QIP, which opened on November 16 and closed on November 19, attracted participation from more than 60 investors. The company allotted 16.02 crore equity shares at Rs 156 per share to 33 investors.

The issue price represented a 3.1 per cent discount to the floor price of Rs 161.03 per share, calculated in accordance with Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) regulations.

Who participated in Urban Company's QIP?

The QIP saw participation from domestic mutual funds, insurance companies and global institutional investors. Of the 33 investors that received share allotments, 13 did not hold shares in Urban Company on the date of the issue.

New investors included SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, Kotak Mutual Fund and Nippon India Mutual Fund.

Domestic insurance companies participating in the issue included HDFC Life, Bajaj Life Insurance and Edelweiss Life.

Global institutional investors that participated included Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Pictet, Amundi, Norges Bank Investment Management, Manulife, Dymon Asia and Millennium. Domestic investment firm Premji Invest was also among the participants.

How will Urban Company use the QIP proceeds?

According to the placement document, Urban Company will deploy the net proceeds across several business requirements, including strengthening the supply ecosystem for InstaHelp by UC, its service offering.

The company has also earmarked funds for brand marketing, business promotion, technology and cloud infrastructure, and training infrastructure for service professionals.

Other proposed uses include research and development of native products, potential acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

Morgan Stanley India Company acted as the lead book-running manager for the QIP, with Kotak Mahindra Capital Company and Emkay Global Financial Services also serving as book-running managers.

data.title: DGCA Gives SpiceJet Seven Days To Explain Operational, Regulatory Lapses
data.description:
The aviation regulator has flagged a majority of the airline's fleet being grounded, rising flight cancellations, unpaid penalties and uncertainty over mandatory insurance coverage

The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued a seven-day show-cause notice to SpiceJet, seeking an explanation for repeated operational disruptions and alleged violations of aviation regulations, as the airline faces mounting financial and operational challenges.

In a notice, the regulator raised concerns over the airline's deteriorating operational performance, including declining on-time performance, increasing flight delays and cancellations, and failure to operate services according to its approved schedule. The airline has also been asked to explain inadequate passenger facilitation measures amid the disruptions.

One of the key concerns flagged by the DGCA is that a majority of SpiceJet's aircraft remain grounded and that the airline has not submitted a credible plan for bringing them back into service.

The regulator has also cited concerns raised by overseas aviation authorities over operational disruptions linked to delayed payments to service providers.

Regulatory Compliance Concerns

The notice also flags SpiceJet's repeated non-compliance with Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDG), despite earlier enforcement action and a penalty imposed in May. The airline has been asked to explain its failure to meet eligibility requirements for operating scheduled international services.

The DGCA has further sought an explanation for the non-payment of an earlier penalty despite repeated reminders. Uncertainty surrounding the renewal of mandatory insurance coverage has also been cited as a concern.

SpiceJet has been directed to submit its response within seven days of the notice. The regulator may take further action depending on the airline's response and its compliance with the requirements.

Financial Strain Deepens

The regulatory action comes as SpiceJet continues to face financial constraints and a contraction in its operations. Its domestic market share declined to 0.6 per cent in September from 1.2 per cent in August.

The airline's board approved a proposal on 18 November to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore through equity shares or other permitted securities to strengthen its financial position and support its revival plans.

The proposed fundraise is intended to help the airline restore grounded aircraft, rebuild operational capacity and strengthen its balance sheet.

data.title: TSX slips as precious metal prices weigh, eyes sharpest weekly decline in over 6 months

data.title: Anthropic's stock slides closer to IPO price and drags down the AI trade
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Anthropic's inability to hold its opening stock price has been seen as 'bad for the rest of tech'

Anthropic finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday.

There was no honeymoon period for Anthropic after its record-breaking initial public offering.

Shares of the AI company are down more than 9% in morning action on Friday, making for a gloomy second day of trading. Anthropic's stock (ANT) is at $88.16, well below its $111.50 opening price, and falling closer toward its $83 IPO price.

It's a downbeat sign for the broader technology ecosystem as well, with AI stocks taking a beating across the board. Among notable losers are shares of Sandisk (SNDK), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell Technologies (DELL), Nebius Group (NBIS) and Arm Holdings (ARM).

"The vast majority of this continued selling pressure in the last 24 hours feels more to do with" the Anthropic IPO than it does with some less-than-perfect earnings reports in the technology sector, according to Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza.

He wrote in a note to clients that Anthropic's inability to hold its opening price and the downward pressure in Friday's premarket action is being viewed as "bad for the rest of tech."

Anthropic's IPO was seen as a tentpole event for the AI trade. The company finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Friday's action brings that down to $1.16 trillion.

"Anthropic's strong debut alongside a falling technology sector suggests investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, said in emailed comments.

Some analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic's stock after Thursday's close, chiming in with mixed views.

"We are cautious, not negative," wrote Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg, who launched coverage of shares with a neutral rating.

He called Anthropic an "incredible company," but also one "asking for an incredible leap of faith by investors."

"We think the company will need time to grow into its valuation and answer some very big questions about its growth trajectory," he continued. For instance, the company saw 43% revenue growth from the second quarter to the third quarter. That compared with a much faster 144% growth rate from the first quarter to the second quarter.

Goldberg referred to that as a "worrying" deceleration. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years," he added.

William Blair's Arjun Bhatia was more upbeat, calling Anthropic a "generational company driving a generational technology shift" as he began his own coverage of the stock with an outperform rating.

"Questions about the future are worth asking, even those that don't have an answer at this point," he wrote.

But at the same time, he and his team "don't want to miss the forest for the trees."

"We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies," Bhatia wrote. "Over the next decade, we think Anthropic is only going to become more important and consume a greater portion of enterprise spend," meaning it will command more of the budget that businesses have to allocate toward technology.

-Emily Bary

data.title: MySize Reports 21% Nine-Month Revenue Growth as Third-Quarter Revenue Falls 28%
data.description:
MySize reported revenue of $7.32 million for the first nine months of 2026, up approximately 21% year over year, while third-quarter revenue declined 28% to $1.86 million. The company reported a third-quarter net loss of $1.80 million and said it expects to need additional capital, with substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. MySize also announced a workforce reduction at its Naiz Fit subsidiary and is evaluating potential acquisitions in defense technology.

Financial Highlights

  • Third-quarter revenue was $1.86 million, down approximately 28% from $2.57 million a year earlier; the decline primarily reflected lower Amazon sales associated with reduced inventory availability.
  • Third-quarter gross profit was $591,000, compared with $1.01 million, and gross margin was 31.8%, down from 39.2%.
  • Third-quarter operating loss was $1.68 million, compared with $1.36 million; net loss was $1.80 million, compared with $1.34 million.
  • Nine-month revenue increased approximately 21% to $7.32 million from $6.06 million. Gross profit was $2.50 million, compared with $2.55 million, while gross margin was 34.2%, down from 42.1%.
  • Nine-month operating loss was $4.80 million, compared with $3.00 million, and net loss was $5.03 million, compared with $2.85 million. Operating cash use was $3.04 million; at September 30, cash and cash equivalents were $2.28 million, alongside $130,000 in restricted cash.

Business Highlights

  • SaaS Solutions revenue grew 25% year over year in the third quarter, with gross margin of approximately 82%.
  • Resale platform revenue increased approximately 19% year over year, from $347,000 to $413,000.
  • In September, MySize reduced the Naiz Fit workforce by approximately 50% as part of an operational restructuring. The company estimates the initiative will produce approximately $793,000 in annualized gross cost savings.
  • MySize completed a private placement in September, raising approximately $2.5 million in gross proceeds and $2.12 million in net proceeds.
  • The company continued evaluating potential defense technology acquisitions as part of its diversification initiative. Any transaction would depend on due diligence, financing, definitive agreements, and required approvals.

Original SEC Filing: My Size, Inc. [ MYSZ ] - 8-K - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: ICE Canada Morning Comment: ICE Canola Futures Softer
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE canola futures were posting small losses Friday morning as values continued to chop around in narrow, rangebound trade.

The January contract was down $2.50 at C$774.50 per tonne in early activity.

Overnight losses in Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil accounted for some spillover selling pressure.

Canada exported 141,000 tonnes of canola during the week ended Nov. 15, which was roughly half of what moved the previous week, reported the Canadian Grain Commission.

However, marketing-year-to-date exports of 2.66 million tonnes remain well ahead of the 1.83 million tonnes exported by the same point in 2025-26.

Updated supply/demand estimates from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada included only minor adjustments to the canola balance sheet, with projected 2026-27 ending stocks lowered to 1.87 million tonnes from 1.97 million in October.

Projected exports for the year were left unchanged at 7.7 million tonnes, while domestic usage was raised by 100,000 tonnes to 14.5 million.

About 14,300 canola contracts had traded as of 8:46 a.m. ET.

data.title: Vallourec Shares Plunge on Disappointing Guidance, U.S. Concerns
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Vallourec shares fell sharply Friday after guidance for the final quarter of the year disappointed investors and the company flagged an operational issue in the U.S.

Shares were 11% lower in afternoon European trade.

The French manufacturer of tubes and pipes to the oil and gas, auto and other industrial markets said that the temporary operational issue relates to a subcontractor and contributed to lower-than-expected sequential improvement in its U.S. business in the third quarter.

At the same time, while crude exports and drilling activity have picked up in the Middle East, a recent deterioration in the maritime security situation in the region has created logistical disruptions and higher costs that led to delays in deliveries and invoicing.

"With tube inventories in the region largely depleted, the need to prioritize tube shipments to maintain drilling operations and ensure adequate stocks is becoming critical," Chief Executive Officer Philippe Guillemot said in a statement.

The renewed escalation in the Middle East has clouded visibility and heightened near-term shipment risks, while the temporary operational issue in the U.S. business is also expected to constrain an improvement in the business that was expected in the fourth quarter, Guillemot added.

Vallourec expects group fourth-quarter earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization of between $170 million and $210 million.

Analysts at Jefferies said in a note to clients that Friday's share price reaction appears largely due to the uncertainty around the U.S. operational issue. Nevertheless, the bank said the extent of the price fall seems overdone, given that many investors acknowledged that consensus appeared too high amid the continued Middle East logistics risk.

"Whilst we had been cautious on the 4Q guide, which is -25% versus consensus, the extent of today's reaction surprises us."

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com
